meta.source_of_truth: Google Docs (Gadgets, Gear and Gunships; Rebels & Recruits; Enemies). This file is the machine-readable copy.
meta.edit_workflow: python3 tools/db/build.py export-xlsx  ->  edit in Google Sheets  ->  download .xlsx  ->  python3 tools/db/build.py import-xlsx <file>

rules.note: Base Target Number = tn_base - ROUNDUP(size / tn_size_divisor), never below tn_floor. A zero-skill pilot in that ship has exactly this TN.
Two size steps = one TN point.
Lowest base TN, so very large ships still need a roll.
Rebels & Recruits: skills are capped at 50.
Skill bonus = FLOOR(skill / skill_per_bonus) + FLOOR(level / level_per_bonus). Applies to Aim (to hit) and Focus (to not be hit). Proposed, not yet in the docs.
See skill_per_bonus.
Rebels & Recruits: levels 1 to 20, all rebels start at level 1.
Rebels & Recruits: a rebel levels up at 100 XP.
Initiative is a pilot/soldier/marine stat from 1 to 6. 6 moves last but shoots first. Traits and morale may push the effective value outside this range.
See initiative_min.
Chance that each usable item a downed enemy carries is left on the body for the taking. 1 = always. Kit with live FALSE (riot shield, baton) stays with the body either way. DESIGN_BLOCKERS M-24.
Sundering weapons multiply the damage they do to an armour bar by this (Gear doc: especially effective against armour). Ground Combat doc: armour. My number.
Piercing weapons send this share of each hit past the armour bar straight to health while the armour lasts. My number.
What a riot shield soaks from the front before it breaks (Gear doc: until it breaks). My number.
Ship and vehicle repair, % of hull a day, with no Workshop built.
Repair, % a day, with a Workshop and nobody on its post.
Materials each damaged ship or vehicle costs per day of repair.
XP a day for a rebel in the Training Hall.
XP a day for a Support rebel working in their home room (1 XP = a level). Support Specialties doc: they learn by working.
XP a day for a Support rebel running a niche Job (replaces support_room_xp that day).
Staff learn this much faster while their Lead Specialist is a higher level (doc: 50% faster).
Days in the classroom to train a Support rebel's niche (level 3).
Credits to train a niche, as for a soldier or pilot specialty.
Injured rebels each Doctor treats at once (Treatment).
Treatment: treated rebels heal this much faster with a level 1 Doctor (0.5 = 50%).
Treatment: ...rising to this at level 19.
Stabilise: chance a rebel who would die survives in Critical Condition, with a level 1 Doctor on base.
Stabilise: ...rising to this at level 19.
Days of recovery in Critical Condition (it only heals under Treatment).
Intel a day per Intelligence Center room while an Intelligence Officer works there.
Sources each Intelligence Officer processes (Processing).
Processing: extra Intel from a processed Source (0.25 = +25%).
Repairs: % of hull a day for the ship or vehicle a level 1 Mechanic is working on (others repair at repair_rate_workshop).
Repairs: ...rising to this at level 19.
Salvage: extra Materials from missions with a level 1 Mechanic as Department Head (0.1 = +10%).
Salvage: ...rising to this at level 19.
Maintenance: chance a Med Pack, grenade or charge used on a mission comes back, level 1 Technician.
Maintenance: ...rising to this at level 19.
Supply-producing Sources each Logistics Specialist handles (Supply Handling).
Supply Handling: extra Supplies from a handled Source (0.25 = +25%).
Inventory Control: extra Arsenal slots with a level 1 Logistics Specialist as Department Head.
Inventory Control: ...rising to this at level 19.
Tutoring: a tutored Support rebel learns this much faster.
Flags of local Support a Diplomatic Task (Outreach) raises, before outreach_bonus.
Outreach: a Diplomat's team raises Support this much more (doc: 25% faster).
Mission Support: Cool a supported squad starts with (also Peak Condition and Rallying Cry).
Mission Support: added to an unflown (sent) mission's chance of success.
Drill: share of specialty training time an Instructor saves (also Conditioning).
Drill: rebels training in the Training Hall learn this much faster with an Instructor supervising.
Rehab: extra recovery for a rebel in rehab, on top of Treatment.
Strength Programme: days per programme.
Strength Programme: skill points a programme adds (Agility or Constitution).
Supplies a basic prosthetic costs (Prosthetics); Rapid Fitting halves it.
Fighter Tuning and Heavy Frames: days the ship is in the Workshop.
Heavy Frames: hull added.
Pre-flight Checks: shield added to a prepared ship's front shield.
Haggler: Black Market price cut (0.15 = 15%).
Fence: gear sold from the Arsenal fetches this many times the usual price.
Broadcasts, Recruitment Drive and Hero Stories: days a campaign runs.
Symbol of the Revolution: extra Revolution progress (0.15 = 15%).
Data Tap: Intel a day from a tap.
Data Tap: network exposure added a day by a tap.
Days to fit a basic prosthetic (Prosthetics); Rapid Fitting halves it.

manufacturers.name: Bhord
manufacturers.description: Makes the equivalent of AK-47s: the cheap and effective kind of small arms and ship weapons.

manufacturers.name: Fightstar
manufacturers.description: A mainstay weapons manufacturer for the civilian market that found its niche selling to mercenaries, which has spread to pirates and gangs alike.

manufacturers.name: Patriot
manufacturers.description: Makes personal weapons and armour for the Hegemony. Their owner has drunk the koolaid and hates 'those damn revs'. It's a big contract, so their kit is well made and advanced, but cost effective.

manufacturers.name: Devlin & Son
manufacturers.description: A full range of ballistic personal firearms, from pistols and SMGs through assault rifles, shotguns and heavy weapons. Old, dependable and slightly obsessed with mechanical simplicity: the galaxy's Colt or Remington.

manufacturers.name: LMC (Lark-Murray Corporation)
manufacturers.description: Top of the line small arms, gadgets and ship weapons, with partnerships with big science labs. Advanced, expensive weaponry.

manufacturers.name: MenDon
manufacturers.description: Practical, uncomplicated and sturdy vehicles and ships for salt of the earth people. They might not be lookers, but they get the job done.

manufacturers.name: Aerostar
manufacturers.description: Maker of sleeker, premium ships and vehicles, such as racing ships, yachts, cruisers, transports and more.

manufacturers.name: Varrondow Conglomerate
manufacturers.description: Their owner is best friends with the Empress, and is responsible for producing the main line of small combat craft and ship weapons for the Hegemony's squadrons.

manufacturers.name: AutoCom
manufacturers.description: Producer of untold millions of gadgets, Autos, Bots and Drones used throughout the Hegemony, especially by its security forces and military. Rumours of sentience emerging on the factory lines are entirely unfounded.

manufacturers.name: Praxon
manufacturers.description: Industrial equipment manufacturer that accidentally became a major arms supplier to pirates and criminals. Their protective gear, mining lasers, cutting tools, gadgets and industrial exosuits have all found extremely creative applications in the hands of these good for nothings, and rebels.

manufacturers.name: Helix
manufacturers.description: Medical equipment and pharmaceuticals, from battlefield medkits to sophisticated surgical machines. Their products are excellent. Their prices are not.

manufacturers.name: BLAMCo
manufacturers.description: Producer of some of the finest explosives known to mankind. Accept no imitations. Will not be knowingly under-exploded by a competitor.

manufacturers.name: General Astronautics
manufacturers.description: Huge military-industrial corporation making basically every type of serious, larger military spacecraft for the Hegemony: frigates, destroyers, carriers, support ships. Very boring name, extremely enormous corporation.

manufacturers.name: Nomad
manufacturers.description: A complete range of frontier-oriented armour and protective equipment, designed for settlers, prospectors, mercenaries and people who expect to have to repair it themselves.

manufacturers.name: Rook
manufacturers.description: Broad manufacturer of practical personal protection: body armour, helmets, tactical suits, environmental protection. Affordable and repairable.

size_scale.reference: Speeder bike, power armour, small drone
Heavy fighter, gunship, bomber, large drone

weapons.name: BLS-T Light Repeaters
weapons.notes: Stats are the current Cross plasma. The per-ship plasma values in the game today (Talon 9-15, Mote 6-10, Fledgling 7-12, Scimitar 8-14) all collapse into this one weapon.

weapons.name: Missiles
weapons.special_rules: Heavy warhead. Needs a lock. Guidance bonus per lock level.
weapons.notes: Ammo 2 as on the Cross and Scimitar today (the Talon carried 1).

weapons.name: Door Mounted Gun
weapons.special_rules: Bypasses shields. Can crit through armour. Wild and unguided. Needs a Gunner Position; enables Door Gunner Support in Ground Missions.
weapons.notes: Stats are the Graf's current ballistic guns (10-16, 10 rounds).

weapons.name: Sentry Pulse Emitter
weapons.notes: Placeholder name. Damage carried over from the RQ-7 Sentry's plasma.

weapons.name: Monitor Pulse Emitter
weapons.notes: Placeholder name. Damage carried over from the Drone Monitor's plasma.

weapons.name: Pursuer Pulse Cannon
weapons.notes: Placeholder name. Damage carried over from the Drone Pursuer's plasma.

weapons.name: Clamper Pulse Emitter
weapons.notes: Placeholder name. Damage carried over from the Drone Mag-Clamper's plasma.

ships.name: FT-4 Cross
ships.description: This MenDon multirole patrol craft is a practical workhorse designed for frontier law enforcement and small company security. It is cheap but with maintenance can last for decades.

ships.name: SF-11 Talon
ships.description: Designed principally for performance and racing, the Talon is a highly regarded small single seater. On the frontier, it's been adapted into a makeshift interceptor, even though its frame can't take very heavy hits.

ships.name: VC Mote
ships.description: A product for use by Hegemony Security forces to maintain day to day order, the Mote is a simple and lightly armed craft for dealing with cargo stops and chasing stolen ships. It is still a symbol of dreary Hegemon repression.
ships.notes: Enemies doc calls it the VC Mote Patrolcraft.

ships.name: VT-2 Fledgling
ships.description: An older, smaller fighter no longer in active Hegemon service, the VT-2 is typically now used to train the next generation of suicidally brave naval pilots. Pirates occasionally steal and revive them from the scrapyards.

ships.name: VK-3 Scimitar
ships.description: An advanced multi-role fighter, the Scimitar is a currently active model flown by wing commanders in the navy.

ships.name: Graf Hauler
ships.special_rules: 1 Gunner Position (enables 'Door Gunner Support' fire support option in Ground Missions if the player adds 'Door Mounted Gun' to one of its weapon slots)
ships.description: Nicknamed 'ol Gran', the Graf Hauler is a part of life in much of the Hegemony. This depending light hauler is cheap, sturdy and reliable to get cargo or people from A to B. It is very commonly converted into a combat dropship by militia, pirates and other scum.
ships.notes: The game currently calls it Graf Type 1 Hauler. Description is verbatim from the Gear doc, including 'depending' (dependable?).

ships.name: RQ-7 Sentry
ships.special_rules: Drone: no pilot. Never panics or flees.
ships.description: A flight computer with a gun.
ships.notes: In the game but not in the Enemies doc. Carried over and converted to the new format; delete if unwanted.

ships.name: Drone Monitor
ships.special_rules: Drone: no pilot. Never panics or flees. Calls in one Drone Pursuer the first time a rebel ship comes within 900.
ships.description: Drone starfighter that patrols civilian routes for trouble and crime. Individually weak, typically summons better drone reinforcements.
ships.notes: Converted from game values. Hard points set to 0 for drones; change if drones should be modifiable.

ships.name: Drone Pursuer
ships.special_rules: Drone: no pilot. Never panics or flees.
ships.description: Drone starfighter that usually deals with hostile space situations day to day.

ships.name: Drone Mag-Clamper
ships.special_rules: Drone: no pilot. Never panics or flees. Mag-Clamp: as its action, clamps an enemy ship within 650 in clear line of sight, reducing that ship's top speed by 2 for 2 rounds.
ships.description: Larger drone ship that uses powerful magnets and tech to restrain and slow ships.
ships.notes: Converted from game values. It cannot make hard turns, as today.

ships.name: Fuel Depot
ships.special_rules: Structure: stationary, takes no turns, has no subsystems (a crit damages the hull directly). Destroying every depot ends the Cook the Depots mission.
ships.description: Sixty thousand tonnes of patrol fuel in a can.
ships.notes: Size 12 gives base TN 6; it is 8 in the game today.

pilots.name: Sera Kest
pilots.notes: Seed values. Aim = old aim x 10; Presence = old cool / 2; Cunning is a placeholder equal to Aim. Initiative = her old ship's value.

pilots.name: Joss Marrek
pilots.notes: Seed values, same rules as Sera. Traits: reckless, his Character Trait in the campaign (the old space-only "Ace Training" did nothing; his loop is in his maneuvers).

pilots.name: Petra Voss
pilots.notes: Seed values, same rules as Sera.

pilots.name: Cmdt. Dral Vex
pilots.notes: Focus held at 30 (not 50) so the boss lands at TN 13 rather than 15. The Veteran trait still adds +1 initiative in code, giving the 4 he has today.

pilots.name: Cadet Ilo
pilots.notes: Level 0 in the game today; all levels now start at 1. Focus 0 because the Fledgling's base TN (10) is already above today's 9.

pilots.name: Patrol Pilot
pilots.notes: Generic pilot the game summons in the Cook the Depots mission.

pilots.name: RQ-7 Sentry core
pilots.notes: Built-in flight computer. Focus 0 and level 1 means TN equals the size base, which matches today's value.

pilots.name: Drone Pursuer core
pilots.notes: As the Sentry core. Aim 20 matches the summoned Pursuer today.

pilots.name: Depot Core
pilots.notes: Seed: a structure's stand-in pilot. It never moves or shoots; Presence 25 matches the nerve 50 it had in code.

starting_fleet.name: Dustfall
starting_fleet.notes: The Cross stolen in onboarding (Steal the Cross). Stock Cross plus a missile system in the second slot.

starting_fleet.name: Marta
starting_fleet.notes: The derelict Graf Joss restores. Starts with a Door Mounted Gun, per the designer.

items.name: Akli AR
items.description: About as common a sight in the universe as space ants, this timeless workhorse model can be found in the hands of militias, pirates, outlaws and revolutionaries.
items.notes: Gear doc fire modes (automatic, semi-auto) not built yet.

items.name: Cowboy No.4
items.description: A simple but dependable sidearm revolver for the gun-needer rather than the gun-fanatic.

items.name: Varmint Shotgun
items.description: Great for keeping those Blagabloops off your carrots.

items.name: Longhorn ’28
items.description: A long range marksman rifle designed for bringing down space critters and creatures.
items.notes: The ground scene called it “Longhorn ’28 Hunting Rifle”. Gear doc traits not built yet: Steady.

items.name: Improvised Rocket Launcher
items.description: Watch that backblast.
items.notes: Crafted: no maker. Gear doc Knockback not built yet. No mechanics for an owned one yet (DESIGN_BLOCKERS M-17).

items.name: Improvised Plasma SMG
items.description: An unstable plasma core with some questionable metal tubes: a ferocious, high damage, if unstable, close quarters weapon.
items.notes: Crafted: no maker. Gear doc traits: automatic, Unstable. No mechanics yet (DESIGN_BLOCKERS M-17).

items.name: Repurposed Mining Laser
items.description: Large two handed weapon that delivers a powerful sweep attack. Requires a recharge.
items.notes: A deployable in the Gear doc: a cone sweep and a Recharge action. No mechanics yet (DESIGN_BLOCKERS M-17).

items.name: Razorrat LMG
items.description: This deployable light machine gun can be set up on the ground to provide a lethal option against infantry.
items.notes: Stats are my numbers. Gear doc: automatic, Piercing, Heavy. Carried in the Back slot and set up with Deploy; Steal the Cross has one on the landing pad (it replaced the laser turret).

items.name: EG-55 Peacekeeper Carbine
items.notes: Gear doc: Fightstar plasma (DESIGN_BLOCKERS C-23, settled with the art). Loot only: Hegemony issue.

items.name: ST Stiletto
items.description: A sporting carbine with vicious plasma shots.
items.notes: Stats are my numbers. Gear doc: Fightstar plasma carbine, semi-auto, Sundering. Art from the October 5 art handoff.

items.name: HG-40
items.description: Heavy pistol used by security and police.
items.notes: Stats are placeholders copied from the Cowboy No.4 (DESIGN_BLOCKERS C-24).

items.name: Power Baton
items.description: A simple looking stick made of a dense material for extra battering power. Simple melee weapon used by security forces.
items.notes: Gear doc: melee (blunt), Stunning. No mechanics yet (DESIGN_BLOCKERS M-17).

items.name: Riot Shield
items.description: Defensive portable cover that negates incoming damage. Until it breaks, anyway.
items.notes: A deployable in the Gear doc: Deploy moves it into the hands in place of the primary; it soaks hits from the front until it breaks (the riot_shield_hp rule), and a broken one is used up. Enemy shieldmen carry it ready.

items.name: Auto Plasma Hand
items.notes: Crafted from an Auto (Gear doc): dropped by Auto enemies only. Placeholder stats copied from the Cowboy No.4 (DESIGN_BLOCKERS C-24).

items.name: Frontier Hardhat
items.description: A solid choice for avoiding common workplace injuries. Looks great in camo.

items.name: Cowboy Hat
items.description: “Howdy, partner.”
items.notes: Cosmetic only (Gear doc): no armour.

items.name: Baseball Cap
items.description: “Frontier Fashion”
items.notes: Cosmetic only (Gear doc): no armour.

items.name: Police Helmet
items.description: Extra safety for a copper’s cranium.

items.name: Police Vest
items.description: First line of defence between you and an angry mob.

items.name: Auto Head-Helm
items.description: A scavenged Auto’s head turned into a helmet. Those Auto heads are rather sturdy. No wonder they’re made of them.
items.notes: Crafted: no maker.

items.name: Med Pack
items.description: Used to treat critical injuries and downed-but-not-dead characters. Consumed when used.
items.notes: Helix, from the October 5 art handoff (clinical white and teal, the double-helix mark).

items.name: BLAM Frag Grenade
items.description: Very cheap and efficient frag grenade from BLAMCo, but only really effective at anti-personnel.

items.name: BLAM C90 Explosive Charge
items.description: A pretty damn effective charge for blasting things, and great value.
items.notes: Saves and the art kit call it c90.

items.name: Stim
items.description: Heals when used. Consumed when used.
items.notes: No mechanics as a carried item yet (DESIGN_BLOCKERS M-17). Helix, from the October 5 art handoff (clinical white and teal, the double-helix mark).

items.name: Molotov Cocktail
items.description: “Some things never change, do they?”
items.notes: Crafted: no maker. Sets an area and anyone in it on fire until they Extinguish. No mechanics yet (DESIGN_BLOCKERS M-17).

items.name: Guardian Angel Drone
items.description: A cheeky, tiny, flying drone that will intercept a shot on behalf of the user when active.
items.notes: Crafted: no maker. Intercepts one attack for the user. No mechanics yet (DESIGN_BLOCKERS M-17).

items.name: Auto Core Improvised Charge
items.description: A core from an Auto with plastic putty and a lot of explosive additional chemicals. Serves as an explosive charge when one is needed.
items.notes: Crafted: no maker. No mechanics yet (DESIGN_BLOCKERS M-17).

items.name: Data Limpet
items.description: A palm-sized tap that clamps onto a comm tower and copies every packet that passes. Needs no fuse.

items.name: Bare hands
items.notes: Built in; never owned. Moves to a units table when one exists.

items.name: Riot Fists
items.notes: Built in; never owned. Moves to a units table when one exists.

items.name: Cruiser Pulse Cannon
items.notes: Built in; never owned. Moves to a units table when one exists.

items.name: Dispersal Turret
items.notes: Built in; never owned. Moves to a units table when one exists.

items.name: Strider Autocannon
items.notes: Built in; never owned. Moves to a units table when one exists.

enemies.name: Auto Policebot
enemies.description: A robot policeman intended to be ‘friendly and helpful’, yet usually resorts to violence when civilians don’t comply. Pretty dumb and flimsy.
enemies.notes: Carried a Cowboy before the roster; the Auto Plasma Hand (AutoCom, drop only) matches the art kit and the Gear doc. A hacked one joins as a soldier.

enemies.name: Security Patrolman
enemies.description: Beat cop. Armed with a pistol and uniform, and baton for quelling unruly civilians day to day.
enemies.notes: Pistol = Patriot HG-40 (Hegemony issue). The baton has no rules yet (live FALSE), so it is carried, not swung, and stays on the body.

enemies.name: Security Riot Shieldman
enemies.head: policehelmet
enemies.description: Riot police that wields a riot shield protecting them from the front from all damage.
enemies.notes: Carrying a riot shield is what gives them the frontal shield. Helmet and vest: my pick for riot police (the Gear doc makes them Patriot loot-only kit).

enemies.name: Security Riot Rifleman
enemies.head: policehelmet
enemies.description: Riot police that wields a rifle to deal with unpatriotic terrorists and kidnappers.
enemies.notes: Rifle = EG-55 Peacekeeper Carbine. Drawn as a riot rifleman in a Police Helmet (art handoff).

enemies.name: Auto Riot Bruiser
enemies.description: Riot robot that beats up ne’er-do-wells with its fists. Tankier.
enemies.notes: No art spec yet (DESIGN_BLOCKERS M-21): drawn as a Policebot at 1.25x.

enemies.name: Strider Mk I
enemies.description: Built by AutoCom, the Mk I is a friendly neighbourhood enforcement robotic strider.
enemies.notes: An owned one is the same row (DESIGN_BLOCKERS C-21). Armour 50 came out of its old 240 hp, so it lasts as long as before.

enemies.name: Depot Guard
enemies.notes: Guards the Tithe depot (Steal Fuel). Not in the Enemies doc; the nearest is the Security Patrolman. Two carry carbines and one sits in the tower with a hunting rifle (set on the spawn).

enemies.name: Depot Warden
enemies.notes: Leads the Tithe depot reinforcements. Not in the Enemies doc. Carries a shotgun, as before the roster.

enemies.name: Frontier Sheriff
enemies.head: cowboyhat
enemies.description: The lawman in a frontier town, the sheriff enforces the law as best they are able. That law is Hegemony law though, so really, they’re not all good guys.
enemies.notes: Sheriff Reeve of Dustfall. The vest follows the art kit (Hegemony law, Hegemony issue).

enemies.name: Frontier Deputy
enemies.description: A deputised settler, handed a gun by their sheriff and expected to step up in the moment to serve the law.
enemies.notes: Most carry a Cowboy; some are handed a Peacekeeper Carbine and the tower lookout a hunting rifle (set on the spawn).

enemies.name: Squatter Boss
enemies.notes: Boss Craw, who holds Haven Rock before the rebels take it. Not in the Enemies doc.

enemies.name: Haven Squatter
enemies.notes: Craw’s gang at Haven Rock (the Vult gang). Not in the Enemies doc. Some are tougher or steadier than others (set on the spawn).

enemies.name: Police Cruiser
enemies.description: Floating police car. Security forces use these day to day.
enemies.notes: The driver fires the nose cannon. One you steal joins the vehicle pool. Its armour came out of its old hp (130), so it lasts as long as before.

enemies.name: Riot Dispersal Cruiser
enemies.description: Floating truck. Has a turret that comes out when a riot gets out of control.
enemies.notes: A driver and an exposed turret gunner. Its armour came out of its old hp (170), so it lasts as long as before.

enemies.name: Riot Transport Cruiser
enemies.description: Floating truck. Transports Riot forces into danger zones.
enemies.notes: Unarmed: a driver and a troop bay for three. Its armour came out of its old hp (150), so it lasts as long as before.

market_weights.notes: From the Market/Arsenal handoff. Rows for Revolution Level 2 and up wait on DESIGN_BLOCKERS M-18; until then Level 1 weights apply everywhere.

space_enemies.description: Manned starfighter for day to day operations that require someone smarter than a robot.

space_enemies.bio: Sixty thousand tonnes of patrol fuel in a can.
